study_design: Hospital-based case-control study with an accompanying meta-analysis
reason: The primary study evaluates newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed prostate cancer, and the meta-analysis evaluates prostate cancer generally. The abstract does not analyze high-grade, advanced, metastatic, lethal, or another aggressive incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Newly diagnosed African American men with histologically confirmed prostate cancer (n = 127) and controls (n = 81) were recruited from an urban academic urology clinic in Washington, DC.
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate concerns overall histologically confirmed prostate cancer, not an aggressive subtype. The row is the reciprocal orientation of the reported highest-versus-lowest tertile comparison.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: We observed a non-significant, non-linear increase in prostate cancer when comparing tertiles of zinc intake (OR <6.5 vs 6.5-12.5mg/day 1.8, 95% CI: 0.6,5.6; OR <6.5 vs >12.5mg/day 1.3, 95% CI: 0.2,6.5).
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported outcome is prostate cancer overall, with no aggressive disease definition.
